questions.text: Which kind of therapy goal it is?

options.name: Behavioral Goal
options.description: Answer question: "What I want to do?"

options.name: Emotional Goal
options.description: Answer question: "How I want to feel?"

options.name: Outcome Goal
options.description: Answer question: "What I want to get or have?"

options.name: A way of acting
options.description: How the person wants to behave, again and again, which never gets finished. A single word counts when people usually mean it as acting: adventure, caring, curiosity, excitement, safety.

options.name: A goal
options.description: Something that can be done, reached, ticked off or owned: moving to Italy, a fit body, earning money.

options.name: A feeling
options.description: A state the person wants to feel or stop feeling: calm, happy, in control, not anxious. Only feelings, not actions.

options.name: What others give
options.description: Something other people would have to do, think or give: recognition, respect, being liked.

options.name: A rule
options.description: Something the person feels they must obey, written with should, must, have to, always or never.

options.name: Something to stop
options.description: Not doing something, which a dead person does better: stop procrastinating, stop wasting time.

questions.text: How does the example relate to the value?

options.name: Fits the value
options.description: Something the person can do that acts on the value, even if it is a goal or an activity.

options.name: A feeling
options.description: A state the person wants to feel, not something they do.

options.name: What others give
options.description: Something other people would have to do, think or give.

options.name: Unrelated
options.description: It has nothing to do with the value.
